description: Join a specific (non-home) lot, leaving the current lot. On the wire this is: sidecar issues bot-cmd:probe-lot (city-socket FindLotRequest), confirms FOUND, writes next-lot, then issues bot-cmd:bot-exit-request. The sidecar supervisor detects the clean exit, reads next-lot, and relaunches the bot with FSO_LOT_LOCATION set to the target. The bot joins the target lot via the normal city-connect → JoinLotWithTransitionRequest flow on relaunch. Total elapsed: ~10-15s (probe + disconnect + rejoin). IMPORTANT — `target_lot_location` is the lot **location code** (24-bit coordinate packing, the same value `avatar.LotLocation` returns from `AvatarDataServlet`), NOT the DB lot_id. OQ-3 locked this aliasing trap. I0-2: perception is silent during transit (bot is dead between lots). I0-3: motives travel with the avatar (server-side fso_avatars). NAME-PRIMARY (I0-5): pass --my_name for a bound name of kind 'lot'; --target_lot_location is the hex/decimal escape hatch. Both shapes are mandatory wire-protocol contract.

args.name: my_name
args.description: Your name for the target lot (bound with 'name --as <name> --lot_location 0x...'). Name-primary shape (I0-5). Takes precedence over --target_lot_location when both are present.

args.name: target_lot_location
args.description: Lot location code (hex '0x...' or decimal uint32). Hex fallback when --my_name is absent or unbound. One of my_name or target_lot_location is required.

call_signatures: cf $CF visit-lot --my_name "joao's place"                                            # name-primary: resolve bound lot name → probe → WriteNextLot → bot-exit
cf $CF visit-lot --target_lot_location 0x00F8F0DC                                    # hex fallback: probe → WriteNextLot → bot-exit
common_mistakes: Using lot_id (DB integer) instead of lot_location (24-bit packed coordinate). These are NOT the same — see OQ-3.
Expecting an immediate result — the transition takes ~10-15s. The fulfillment fires when the exit is queued, not when the bot arrives.
Forgetting to bind a lot name first. Use: cf $CF name --as "joao's place" --lot_location 0x00F8F100
perception_hints: Your current lot: perception.lot.lot_id and perception.lot.name
Home detection: go-home returns already_home:true when perception.lot.lot_id matches your home lot location
Probe status in response: probe_status field ('FOUND' means lot was open and reachable)
refuse_conditions: --my_name not bound or not kind='lot' → ok:false
probe-lot returns NOT_OPEN or error → ok:false with probe_status field
